Dwayne Kenneth Schintzius (October 14, 1968 – April 15, 2012) was an American National Basketball Association (NBA) basketball player.
Dwayne Schintzius was born in Brandon, Florida.
Dwayne Schintzius attended the University of Florida.
Dwayne Schintzius helped lead the Florida Gators men's basketball program to its first three NCAA tournament appearances as an all-conference center.
Dwayne Schintzius was selected in the first round of the 1990 NBA draft (24th overall) by the San Antonio Spurs.
Dwayne Schintzius played for six different NBA teams over ten seasons in the league, mainly as a reserve player.
Off the court, Dwayne Schintzius was known for his distinctive mullet-style haircut that he called "the lobster".
Off the court, Dwayne Schintzius had an abrasive behavior.
Dwayne Schintzius performed as a Russian basketball player in the 1996 comedy film Eddie.
In 2009, Dwayne Schintzius was diagnosed with a rare form of leukemia.
After treatment and a brief remission, Dwayne Schintzius died from complications of the disease in 2012.
Dwayne Schintzius was born in Brandon, Florida, a suburb of Tampa.
Dwayne Schintzius attended Brandon High School.
Dwayne Schintzius played for the Brandon Eagles high school basketball team.
Together with teammate Toney Mack, Dwayne Schintzius led the Eagles to a Class 4A state runner-up finish as a sophomore.
Together with teammate Toney Mack, Dwayne Schintzius led the Eagles to another Final Four berth as a junior.
As a senior, Dwayne Schintzius averaged 21.1 points and 17 rebounds per game.
As a senior, Dwayne Schintzius was a finalist for Florida's Mr. Basketball award.
As a senior, Dwayne Schintzius was recognized as a high school All-American by McDonald's.
As a senior, Dwayne Schintzius was recognized as a high school All-American by Parade magazine.
Dwayne Schintzius received athletic scholarship offers from many top college programs.
Unlike most top Florida high school basketball prospects up to that point, Dwayne Schintzius chose to stay in-state and attend the University of Florida.
Dwayne Schintzius played for the Florida Gators men's basketball team from 1987 to 1990 under head coach Norm Sloan.
Dwayne Schintzius started at center for the Gators beginning early in his freshman season.
By the end of Dwayne Schintzius's junior season (1988–89), he had led the Gators in scoring, rebounding, and free-throw percentage over at least one full season.
Dwayne Schintzius set the program's record for blocked shots.
At the end of his junior year, Dwayne Schintzius's season blocked shot totals ranked first, second, and third in school history.
The Gators had never been invited to the NCAA basketball tournament in over seven decades of basketball.
However, they made the field during each of Schintztius's three full seasons with the program.
During his junior year, the Gators won their first-ever regular season Southeastern Conference (SEC) championship.
Dwayne Schintzius was recognized as a first-team All-SEC player after that season.
Dwayne Schintzius was included on multiple All-American lists.
Schintzius occasionally clashed with Coach Sloan.
During his sophomore season, Dwayne Schintzius refused to re-enter a game with a minute left during a game.

During his junior season, Dwayne Schintzius allegedly heard a rude remark from a sidewalk while riding in a car outside a Gainesville nightclub and stormed after the offender wielding a tennis racket.
Dwayne Schintzius later apologized for the incident.
The university's office of student affairs found Dwayne Schintzius guilty of violating the student code of conduct and suspended him for four games.
After returning from that suspension, fans in opposing arenas occasionally threw tennis balls onto the court.
In January 1989, Florida traveled to Nashville to face the Vanderbilt Commodores in a crucial SEC matchup.
Florida lost 72–70 against Vanderbilt.
Florida turned the ball over with only one second left on the clock during the game.
At that point, someone in the Memorial Gymnasium home crowd threw a tennis ball onto the court.
Referee John Clougherty immediately called a technical foul on the Commodores.
Dwayne Schintzius hit both free throws to send the game into overtime.
Dwayne Schintzius then scored the Gators' first seven points in the extra period and Florida won the game 81–78.
Florida went on to capture the program's first SEC regular season championship, beating Vanderbilt by a single game.
Sloan was forced to resign before Dwayne Schintzius's senior season of 1989–90.
Sloan was replaced on an interim basis by former Tennessee coach Don DeVoe.
Dwayne Schintzius skipped DeVoe's first practice with the team along with fellow star Livingston Chatman.
Soon after, he was suspended for alleged involvement in a fraternity house fight.
Without Dwayne Schintzius, the Gators lost sixteen of the seventeen games to end the season and missed the NCAA tournament for the first time since the year before his arrival.
Dwayne Schintzius remains the only player in SEC history to amass more than 1,000 points, 800 rebounds, 250 assists and 250 blocks.
Dwayne Schintzius still holds Florida's career record for blocked shots (272).
Dwayne Schintzius ranks sixth among the program's all-time scoring leaders with 1,624 points.
Despite his personal issues, Dwayne Schintzius was regarded as a good NBA prospect due to his performance on the court.

Schintzius was widely projected as a top five pick before his suspension and during the suspension was seen as a lottery pick being mocked as high as 3rd overall to the late lottery with some seeing Schintzius as the most talented big-man in the draft.
The San Antonio Spurs selected him in the first round (twenty-fourth pick overall) of the 1990 NBA draft.
Dwayne Schintzius injured his back during his rookie season and was traded to the Sacramento Kings for Antoine Carr on September 23, 1991.
Dwayne Schintzius later revealed that Spurs general manager Bob Bass disliked his mullet haircut and told him to cut it, which he did.
Schintzius then sent Bass the shavings in an envelope.
The Kings waived Dwayne Schintzius during the 1991–92 season.
The New Jersey Nets signed Dwayne Schintzius on October 1, 1992.
Dwayne Schintzius' NBA career was severely hampered by injuries, particularly chronic back problems.
He had several surgeries for a spinal disc herniation and often missed long stretches of playing time as he moved from team to team, mostly serving as a reserve center.
He spent three seasons with the New Jersey Nets.
He spent one year with the Indiana Pacers.
He spent one year with the Los Angeles Clippers.
Dwayne Schintzius only played 15 games with the Clippers but did post 15 points in a loss against the Bullets on January 10, 1997.
This game also featured the only three-point make of Schintzius' NBA career.
After missing the entire 1997–98 season due to injury, Dwayne Schintzius played 16 games with the Boston Celtics in 1998–99 before retiring from the NBA.
In eight NBA seasons, he appeared in 217 regular-season games and started 33 of them.
He later came out of retirement to play in the minor leagues.
Dwayne Schintzius played for the Mobile Revelers of the NBA's Development League in 2001–02.
He last played for the Brevard Blue Ducks of the United States Basketball League (USBL) in 2003.
Dwayne Schintzius played Ivan Radovadovitch, a fictional Georgian player for the New York Knicks, in the 1996 comedy movie Eddie.
Several other actual NBA players were also featured as members of the Knicks and other real NBA teams in the film.
Dwayne Schintzius later appeared in local commercials.
At the trial of his former New Jersey Nets teammate Jayson Williams, Dwayne Schintzius testified that he witnessed Williams kill his own dog with a shotgun.
In November 2009, Dwayne Schintzius was diagnosed with chronic myelomonocytic leukemia.
With a bone marrow donation from his brother Travis, Dwayne Schintzius underwent bone marrow transplantation at the Moffit Cancer Center in Tampa on January 12, 2010.
The procedure was considered a success.
Dwayne Schintzius struggled through several difficult rounds of chemotherapy until being declared cancer-free in July 2010.
In early 2012, Dwayne Schintzius continued to suffer from complications and required a second bone marrow transplant.
On April 15, 2012, Dwayne Schintzius died at the Moffit Cancer Center from respiratory failure; he was 43 years old.
